newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean shares seen cautious after rebound.
newsitem.headline: South Korean shares seen cautious after rebound.

text.p: Trading is expected to be cautious on Thursday after the previous day's technical rebound, brokers said.
They added that investors were awaiting the release of economic figures this week.
The composite stock index rose 6.65 points to a close of 722.62 on Wednesday. But despite the climb, most investors had remained sidelined, and volume was a thin 19.9 million.
"The market will see box trading for now," said Choe Seung-wook of Schroders Securities. "The index may gain a little today, but the upside potential is marginal."

Choe forecast that the index would move in a 700 to 730 range for the time being. "It could break 700, depending on the economic figures," he added. "I don't expect much of an improvement in the figures."
Other brokers, however, said investors were already expecting poor economic figures, and that they would not have much impact on the market.

The central bank will release gross domestic product figures for the third quarter on Thursday. On Friday, October current account figures, the consumer price index, oil products demand and an economic forecast for 1997 will be released.
The sale of 360 billion won worth of Korea Telecom shares on Thursday and Friday was seen further pressuring the market's oversupply situation.
Customer deposits, at around 2.4 trillion won, are lagging behind loans out for margin trading, which are valued at 2.8 trillion.
Brokers estimate that 800 billion won in margin loans will have to be paid back in early December.
